newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Key Australian Senator seeks abortion fund end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Key Australian Senator seeks abortion fund end.

text.p: A key Independent senator, on whom the government must rely for its proposed privatization of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp, is seeking an end to public abortion funding, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Sunday.
"These are matters which have been the subject of correspondence with the prime minister (John Howard) and the minister for health (Michael Wooldridge)," Fischer said on Seven Network television.

Earlier, Melbourne's Sunday Age newspaper reported that Independent senator Brian Harradine had asked the government to scrap abortion funding under the national health insurance scheme, Medicare and to stop funding for family planning clinics and tax rebates for in-vitro fertilization.
Neither the newspaper nor Fischer said Harradine had made these demands a condition for supporting the privatization.

Harradine is one of two Independent senators, whose votes are the government's only realistic hope of getting its Telstra privatisation bill through the upper house of parliament. The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate and all non-government parties are opposed to the plan, under which the Liberal-National government would sell a third of Telstra.
